title: AI Change Management and Team Integration

questions.question: Why is AI adoption not finished when a tool is available?
options: Because roles, handoffs, review duties, and behavior changes still need to be clear
Because every tool must be banned first
questions.explanation: AI adoption requires operating routines and role clarity, not only tool access.

questions.question: Which signal is explicitly part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Role impact is one of the adoption signals used by the artifact.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A change-readiness plan with priority, controls, and rationale
questions.explanation: The artifact structures team integration decisions.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: A role map clarifies responsibilities around the changed workflow.

questions.question: When should rollout require stronger controls?
options: When role impact, adoption friction, and governance uncertainty are high
Only when the UI is complex
Only when there are no users
Never; rollout risk is not relevant
questions.explanation: High adoption and governance risk require stronger rollout controls.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the integration plan?
options: To translate AI adoption into team routines, owners, metrics, and controls
questions.explanation: The plan connects change management to concrete operating behavior.
